theme: Zedekiah; the Rechabites; Baruch’s scroll burned
readingInstruction: Read Jeremiah 34:1-36:32. The king breaks a covenant to free slaves. A family called the Rechabites keeps its vow. And King Jehoiakim burns Jeremiah’s scroll in a fire. Read these three stories as a contrast between faithful and unfaithful responses to God’s word.
settingTheScene: These chapters are arranged by theme, not chronology. Chapter 34 is during the siege, when Zedekiah freed the slaves as a covenant and then took them back. Chapters 35 and 36 go back to the days of Jehoiakim, about 605 BC. They show a series of contrasts: a nation that would not keep its word, a clan that did, and a king who could not bear to hear God’s word.
observation: “You recently repented and did what was right in my eyes… but then you turned around and profaned my name when each of you took back his male servant and his female servant” (34:15-16).
“You have not obeyed me by proclaiming liberty, every one to his brother” (34:17).
“The Rechabites, the descendants of Jonadab the son of Rechab, have kept the command that their father gave them, but this people has not obeyed me” (35:16).
“Because you have obeyed the command of Jonadab your father… Jonadab the son of Rechab shall never lack a man to stand before me” (35:18-19).
“Take a scroll and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you” (36:2).
“It may be that the house of Judah will hear all the disaster that I intend to do to them” (36:3).
“Neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words was afraid, nor did they tear their garments” (36:24).
“Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch… who wrote on it all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire” (36:32).
interpretation:
In chapter 34, the people showed a flash of obedience. Under siege, they freed their Hebrew slaves, as the law of Exodus 21 and Deuteronomy 15 required. They made a covenant in the temple, passing between the pieces of a calf. Then, when the Babylonian army withdrew for a moment, they took the slaves back. They had made a vow and broken it. God’s reaction is sharp: they profaned his name. The punishment fits the crime: you did not proclaim liberty, so I proclaim liberty to the sword, the pestilence, and the famine.

Chapter 35 offers a contrast. The Rechabites were a clan who, for generations, had obeyed their ancestor’s rule not to drink wine or build houses. Jeremiah sets wine before them in the temple and invites them to drink. They refuse. They have kept the word of a human father for two hundred years. And God says: you, my people, have not kept the word of your divine Father, spoken persistently. The point is not that abstaining from wine is holy, but that obedience to a spoken word is possible. If a family can keep a command for generations, God’s people should be able to keep his.

In chapter 36, Baruch writes Jeremiah’s words on a scroll and reads it in the temple. Officials are afraid and report it to the king. Jehoiakim sits by the fire in the winter house, and as the scroll is read he cuts it up with a knife and throws it in the fire, column by column. The contrast with Josiah, who tore his clothes at the Book of the Law, could not be clearer. But burning the scroll does not destroy the word. God tells Jeremiah to write it again “and many similar words were added to them.” The word of the LORD is indestructible.
connection: Isaiah 40:8 says, “The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.” Matthew 24:35: “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.” Hebrews 4:12 says the word of God is living and active. John 14:15 says, “If you love me, you will keep my commandments.” James 1:22 says to be doers of the word. Luke 4:18-19 shows Jesus proclaiming liberty to captives.
application:
Examine whether there is a commitment you have made to God or to others that you have taken back.

Ask what you could do to be as faithful to God’s word as the Rechabites were to their father’s.

Pray for the preservation and spread of Scripture, and thank God for your own copy.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that his word cannot be burned.
Ask him to make you faithful in the small commitments.
